answer: The system creates the high-order layer for you: the high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH (super-channel) is created, so on a CHM6 with an OTU configured use 'show odu' to check it exists. The odu command carries the pre-condition that the super-channel must be added before Low Order ODUs can be added. So you add super-channel-<name> (carriers, carrier-mode), then hand-create the low order ODUs with 'add odu-<name> odu-type <ODU4i|ODUflexi|ODU4|ODUflex|ODU0|ODU1|ODU2|ODU2e> parent-odu <HO-ODU> time-slots/opucn-time-slots trib-port-number', then the xcon. Line OTUs are added with a parent, e.g. 'add otu-1-5-L1-1-OTU4-1 parent flexo-group-1-5-L1-1 time-slots 1'. Which is which is visible in the managed-by attribute (system or user, default system on facilities); only user-created facilities can be user deleted. The class attribute reports high-order, low-order or mapped.

The bit error rate test is the 'bert' command (Operational Mode): 'bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=egress test-duration=10', plus bert stop/get/delete. test-signal-type is none, PRBS31, PRBS31NONINV or scrambled-idles (100GE/400GE use scrambled-idles, ODU4 uses PRBS31/PRBS31NONINV); monitoring type adds fec-frames. test-duration is 10 s minimum up to 1000 hrs, 0 means indefinite. Test patterns are injected per facility via test-signal-type / test-signal-direction / test-signal-monitoring on odu-diagnostics and ethernet (none, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9, PRBS31, PRBS31NONINV; direction ingress, egress or both; monitoring default false). Loop the signal back with the loopback attribute on otu, odu, ethernet or optical-carrier: none (default), facility or terminal, with loopback-mode loopback or loopback-and-continue.

Each end needs a secure-entity bound to the local facility and pointed at its far-end peer: 'add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <facility> remote-secure-entity <AID>' where remote-secure-entity is the AID of the remote optical carrier (1830 GX G40), the remote ODU (1830 GX G30) or the remote OTUFlex (CHM7/CHM7X L1 service encryption). The enabled switch defaults to false and must be set true. Tunable policy: re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s (default 28800), re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic or continue-traffic (default continue-traffic), traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s (default 0), alarm-report-control default Inhibited. The SA proposal is fixed: encryption-algorithm aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length key-length-256, integrity-algorithm none, dh-group ecp-521. Certificates must already be imported: the peer-certificate is the trusted remote peer certificate for the L1 encryption secure application, and the local-certificate is the NE's own identity assigned to the secure-application.

The 'telemetry' command configures persistent and dynamic telemetry ('show telemetry', 'set telemetry id <string 0..4096>'); the object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted. 'show subscriptions' lists the subscriptions. Per subscription, 'show current-subscription-<subscription-name>' gives related-session-id, related-dial-out-server, session-type (gnmi-dial-in, gnmi-dial-out-tunnel, gnmi-dial-out-reverse-rpc), session-protocol gnmi, encoding (json, bytes, proto, ascii, json-ietf; default json-ietf), transfer-mode (stream default, once, poll), updates-only (default false) and user-access. What each one watches comes from 'show subscription-path-<subscription-name>/<subscription-path-name>': subscription-path, subscription-path-origin, subscription-path-mode (target-defined default, on-change, sample), sample-interval (default 0; a target-defined stream is auto-adjusted from 0 to 10 seconds), heartbeat-interval (default 0; auto-adjusted to 20 seconds) and suppress-redundant (default true).

At rest the configuration database is encrypted; 'show db-protection-scheme' reports encryption-algorithm xts-aes-256-plain64 (AES-256 in XTS mode, 64-byte block), integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512 or none, integrity-status passed-on-bootup / failed-on-bootup / disabled, and mode encryption-only or encryption-with-integrity, which is changed via the db-migrate RPC. Before you can take a copy, the db-passphrase used for DB snapshot encryption must be configured, either globally with 'set security-policies db-passphrase' (string 40..200) or supplied on the command as 'take-snapshot db-passphrase=***'. It requires a minimum of 40 characters, must not contain dictionary words, and special characters follow the 85-character Z85 set. Automatic DB snapshots are not enabled until it is set. Then 'take-snapshot [db-instance=temp|manual|onehour|oneday|oneweek|rollback] [description=]' (type db-backup default, or system-backup); list results with 'show database'.

Start at the RIB. 'show rib-<rib-name>' lists each RIB by its name key, with the vrf it is bound to and its address-family (ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast); all routes in a RIB belong to the same address family, and for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family, e.g. 'show rib-IPv4'. Then 'show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>' tells you if the prefix made it in and where it came from: source-protocol (OSPF, BGP, static, etc.) and special-next-hop, which is none (normal routes), blackhole or unreachable, default none; for blackhole and unreachable no next-hop is created under the route. 'show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface>' gives the next-hop-address and outgoing interface, e.g. 'show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN'. Which instance it landed in comes from 'show vrf-<name>' (type mgmt or internal, chassis-name); 'show routing' is the umbrella view.

Password acceptance is governed by security-policies. strict-password-check (default true) enforces minimum length 8, at least one lower case letter, one upper case letter, one number and one symbol, and the user name cannot be part of the password; disabled drops all of these except a 1-character minimum. minimum-password-length is 1..200, default 8. enforce-password-history-check (default true) blocks reuse of the previous 5 passwords, with password-history-size 1..200, default 5. These only affect newly defined passwords. Lockout is per user: max-invalid-login is the maximum consecutive invalid login attempts before the account is suspended, range 0..255, default 5, and suspension-time is 0..1440 minutes, default 5; user-status reports lockout, and failed-logins resets to zero on a successful login. security-policies also has disable-user-lockout. To clear a stuck session, run 'show session' for the session-id (<ip-address>:<port>) then 'kill-session <session-id>'; you cannot kill your own session, use exit.

Untouched syslog defaults: remote-logging-switch true, source-address localhost, log-file-message-coalescence true, log-relay false, assignment-method both, niap-compliant-logging false, privacy-mode false, alarm-report-control allowed. Console logging is off by default: log-console enabled defaults to false. Local files: log-file number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, range 1..20, default 10, and when rotating due to max-file-size the oldest files are discarded beyond that count; max-file-size is 1..30 megabytes, default 30; source-facilities defaults to all; severity is informational and above by default; the default system log file cannot be edited or deleted. Remote servers default to port 514, transport udp, message-format rfc5424, origin manual, enabled true. The single switch that turns off everything remote is 'set syslog remote-logging-switch false' - if false, all remote logging destinations are disabled.

What is raised now: 'show current-alarms' (number-of-alarms, last-changed), 'show alarms', and 'show alarm-<alarm-id>' for detail (perceived-severity, reported-time, service-affecting, alarm-category, corrective-action, operator-state/text/name). Manual clearing is 'clear [-f] alarm <alarm-type> [resource=...]'. Most alarms have automatic raise and clear criteria; only a small subset must be acknowledged and cleared by hand, and you find them with 'show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true'. This applies only to system-wide/global alarms not associated with any particular resource. 'set-alarm-state <none|ack|close> [acknowledge-text=] (all-alarms | alarm-id-list=<up to 10 ids>)' changes the operator state. Whether inhibiting reporting drops the already-raised alarms is decided by 'set alarm-control arc-behavior': clear-alarms clears the current alarms when ARC is set to inhibit, leave-alarms (the default) leaves them raised.

The Equipment dashboard shows the sensors: 'status equipment' lists the chassis, the cards per chassis and their subtype, the toms per card, and per equipment the temperature sensors and power values plus presence, oper-state and alarms (for example 'temp 25C | power 2.1/4400 W' on a chassis and 'temp 25C' per card). Narrow it by supplying the chassis id as the filter, e.g. 'status equipment 5'; only existing chassis ids are accepted and wildcards are not supported, so it is either all chassis or exactly one. To get down to one slot use the PM data with a filter, e.g. 'show pm card-1-7', which reports real-time temperature (C) per resource with instant/avg/min/max. Physically the state is reflected in the LEDs: 'show leds', 'show led status' or 'show led-<location>/<name> status', with values not-available (default), off, green, flashing-green, yellow, flashing-yellow, amber, flashing-amber, red, flashing-red, cycling and cycling-with-off.

'show ots-<name>' tells you what the line is doing: span-loss-derived-rx and span-loss-derived-tx are the measured span loss based on OSC including losses external to the fiber, 0..99 dB where 99 dB means OLOS; span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive are the configured fiber losses (0..80 dB, default 0; 99 dB also means not configured on receive, and changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting). span-loss-reference selects which is used, configured or measured, default measured. span-loss-alarm-threshold (0..80 dB, 99 dB, default 99) is set autonomously by the system, is persistent across warm/cold boot, and in measured mode can be forced to update with the update command. span-loss-aging-margin-rx is 0..10.00 dB, default 1.0. What the amplifier is compensating with comes from 'show amplifier-<name>': gain-target and gain-operating (0..40 dB), gain-range-actual, gain-adjustment (-20.00..20.00), input-power-mon and output-power-mon (-99.00..99.00 dBm), tilt-actual and tilt-target, control-mode auto-max-pw (default) or manual, span-loss-control enabled by default, and control-state (converged, fine-tuning, adjusting, stopped).

The chain is trib-ptp (the tributary client physical termination between the transceiver and the immediate protocol layer) into the client protocol facility, ethernet or a client otu, into a low order odu, tied across the node by an xcon (source and destination end-points, payload-type 100GBE/400GBE/OTU4/100G/ODU2/ODU2e, payload-treatment transport, switching, transport-without-fec, regen or regen-switching, network-mapping naming the server layer). The low order ODU sits under a parent-odu high-order ODUCn/ODUCni, which sits under the line otu (OTUCn) and its flexo-group, which binds carriers. From there it becomes optical: line-ptp / super-channel-group, super-channel, optical-carrier, optical-channel. The handover is at line-ptp and optical-carrier: optical-carrier owns frequency, wavelength, tx-power, modulation-format and baud-rate, and line-ptp's line-system-mode (openwave) is the L1 to L0 power control towards the line-system card. Walk it with 'show facilities' and each object's supporting-facilities and supported-facilities.

No, they are two different knobs. A counter crossing a limit is a PM threshold crossing: 'add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter> [low-threshold <value>] [high-threshold <value>]' (numbers, or na, or not-supported; default na), and the TCA must actually be supervised, which is 'set pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> tca-supervision true' per instance or default-tca-supervision on pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> for newly created resources. How loudly an existing fault is reported is alarm severity: 'set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>', for example 'set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor', or 'set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <...>'. 'show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type> default-severity' gives the system default for that alarm type.

Stop it reporting with the card's own alarm-report-control: 'set card-<name> alarm-report-control inhibited' (values allowed and inhibited). Each facility on it has the same attribute, defaulting to allowed on odu, otu, ethernet, ots, trib-ptp, line-ptp, flexo-group and so on, so inhibit those too if you want silence at facility level. You can also put the card into maintenance with 'set card-<name> admin-state maintenance' (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), which shows up in avail-state as maintenance. What happens to the alarms it has already raised is decided system-wide by 'set alarm-control arc-behavior': clear-alarms clears the current alarms when ARC is set to inhibit, while leave-alarms, which is the default, leaves the current alarms in a raised mode. The related alarm-soaking-behavior switch is automatic (default) or no-soak.

A secure application is one that uses an X509v3 certificate as its digital identity, and the certificate it presents is its active-certificate-id: 'set secure-application-<id> active-certificate-id <cert>' (a list, string 0..128, e.g. 'set secure-application-gRPC active-certificate-id certX,certY'). 'show secure-application-<id>' returns type (server or client), active-certificate-id, in-use (the active certificate, a leafref to active-certificate-id), status (enabled or disabled) and verify-client-cert (disabled by default, or required for TLS Mutual Authentication; changes apply only to new TLS connections). Before it will come up the certificate must be imported in PEM format: 'import-certificate local-certificate certificate-name=local-cert-1 <PEM> [passphrase]', plus its CA chain with 'import-certificate trusted-certificate ... [-i]' (-i pulls intermediates from a bundle; roots are installed individually). 'show local-certificate-<id> status' must read valid, not pending-import, expired, revoked or untrusted. For L1 encryption the far-end identity is a peer-certificate.

Pipe the show pm output through the display filter: 'show pm <command flag> | display csv' produces CSV data importable to a spreadsheet such as Excel; 'display xml' and 'display json' are also available. Restrict it to the 15-minute bins with the pm-filter for period, e.g. 'show pm pm-15min | display csv', and add other content filters such as parameter, resource, resource-type or AID (use 'show pm <tab>' for the full list of supported filters). Bin 0 is the current data and bins 1 to n are history, and the bin-to-timestamp mapping is printed with history output. Useful flags: -t for standard table format, -n=<number-of-records> for the maximum records per chassis (default 1000), -s=<skip-records> to page through, -st= and -et= for a timestamp window (format 2021-02-01T10:00:00+01:00), -sbin= and -ebin= for a bin window (default first bin 0, all bins), and -i=<chassis-name>, which may only be given once per command.

Use the PM catalog: 'show pm-catalog <string>' where the string is the catalog name. For example 'show pm-catalog parameter-undersized' returns pm-parameter-undersized with units packets and type counter. It is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The equivalent per-parameter lookup is 'show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]', for example 'show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds', or 'show pm-parameter' for the full list of PM parameters. Both give you the same two facts about the counter name: what unit it is expressed in and whether it is a counter or a gauge.

Turn off data-supervision for that resource with pm-control: 'set pm-control <entity> data-supervision false', for example 'set pm-control pm-resource-card-1-1 data-supervision false'. The entity is the resource to be configured, and data-supervision is real-time data supervision for that resource, valid values true and false, default true. 'show pm-control' lists the configuration for all currently existing resources in the system that support PM data. The per-instance equivalent is 'set pm-resource-<resource> real-time-supervision false' (true/false, default true), which you can read back with 'show pm-resource-<resource> real-time-supervision' along with resource-type, AID and real-time-data-last-reset. Both are available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes. pm-control-entry sets the PM configuration for one particular resource, for one particular period, direction and location, so the key itself gives you exactly that scope: 'set pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> tca-supervision true', for example 'set pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end tca-supervision true'. period is the PM time period (pm-15min, pm-24h), direction is ingress, egress, all or na with default all, and location is all, na, near-end or far-end with default all. The same entry also carries data-supervision (true/false). 'show pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> [supported-parameters] [data-supervision] [tca-supervision]' reads it back; supported-parameters lists the PM parameters that resource type supports for that direction and location, with a maximum of 100 elements.

Query the parameter object: 'show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]', for example 'show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds', or 'show pm-parameter' for the whole list. type is the type of PM parameter and is either counter or gauge. units is one of na, dBm, ms, ps, ps/nm, dB, seconds, packets, events, octets, bits, blocks, times, percent, bit-ratio, C, frames, W, V, A, rpm, ps2, mA, words, cw, nm, bytes, errors or MHz. Example output for pm-parameter-undersized is units packets, type counter. The same two attributes come back from 'show pm-catalog <catalog-name>'. Available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes, use the PM profile's global switch: 'set pm-profile global-data-supervision auto-enabled'. The parameter provides a way to globally enable PM data-supervision without having to toggle it individually. Its two values are auto-enabled, which globally enables the PM data-supervision flag, and manual, which is the default and means the data-supervision flag is controlled via pm-profile-entry or directly per pm-control-entry. Read it back with 'show pm-profile'. The pm-profile object contains information on all resources that support PM data together with their related default configuration; it is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Set the per-resource-type default on pm-profile-entry, which holds the PM configuration per resource type: 'set pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-data-supervision true'. default-data-supervision determines, for newly created resources of this type, whether they have PM data supervision automatically enabled or not (true or false). The companion default-tca-supervision does the same for threshold crossing supervision on newly created resources. In the key, direction is ingress, egress, all or na with default all, location is all, na, near-end or far-end with default all, and period is the PM time period. Read it back with 'show pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> [default-data-supervision] [default-tca-supervision]'. Note that pm-profile global-data-supervision must be left at manual for these per-type defaults to be the controlling setting.

Read real-time-data-last-reset on the pm-resource for that port: 'show pm-resource-<resource> real-time-data-last-reset', for example 'show pm-resource-trib-ptp-1-7-T9'. The attribute is the date and time of the last real time data reset for this resource, in date-and-time format, and if the data was never reset it is the date and time of that resource's creation. The same show also returns resource-type, AID (string 1..64), real-time-supervision (true/false, default true) and the list of pm-control-entry children such as pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end. Clearing is done with 'clear pm real-time' plus optional resource, resource-type, period, location, direction or AID filters to narrow the target.

Create a pm-threshold keyed to that instance: 'add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter> [low-threshold <value>] [high-threshold <value>]', for example a high limit on errored-seconds for one facility's 24-hour ingress near-end bin. resource is the existing system resource instance ID, period is the PM time period (pm-15min, pm-24h), direction is ingress, egress, all or na with default all, location is all, na, near-end or far-end with default all, and parameter is the PM parameter identifier, which can be a counter or a gauge. low-threshold and high-threshold take a number (uint64, int64 or decimal64), or na, or not-supported, and default to na. Use set to change it, 'show pm-threshold-.../<parameter> [low-threshold] [high-threshold]' to read it and delete to remove it. For the threshold to raise a TCA, tca-supervision must be true on the matching pm-control-entry.

Use the PM threshold profile, which holds PM configuration per parameter for a resource type: 'show pm-threshold-profile-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period>/<parameter> [low-threshold] [high-threshold] [default-low-threshold] [default-high-threshold] [min-value] [max-value]'. default-low-threshold and default-high-threshold are the system defined default values for that parameter, and min-value and max-value are the minimum and maximum values for it, which is the range you are allowed to configure. All of these take a number (uint64, int64 or decimal64), or na, or not-supported. low-threshold and high-threshold are the configured values and are the only settable ones: 'set pm-threshold-profile-OTUC14i/ingress/near-end/pm-24h/errored-seconds high-threshold 1200'. In the key, direction is ingress, egress, all or na (default all), location is all, na, near-end or far-end (default all).
